paper.title: Diversified Recommendations for Agents with Adaptive Preferences

settings.name_in_paper: Recommendation menus for adaptive agents (diversity-constrained, EIRD benchmark)
unmapped: Recommender shows a menu of k out of n items (K=n, m=k); the agent picks one item with probability proportional to preference scores M(v) that depend on the agent's memory vector v (normalized histogram of past choices), so choices are history-dependent
Recommender observes the chosen item and its adversarial linear reward
Diversity constraint: empirical item distribution must have entropy at least c (H_c)
Benchmark is the best item distribution in H_c intersected with EIRD(M), the everywhere-instantaneously-realizable set
Learner knows the preference-model class (locally learnable), the dispersion lambda, and the Lipschitz constant of score functions, but not the model itself
settings.definition_quote: In each round t: The Recommender chooses a menu K_t \subset N with |K_t| = k. The Agent chooses item i \in K_t with probability p = s_{v_t,i}/\sum_{j\in K_t} s_{v_t,j} and updates its memory vector ... The Recommender observes receives reward \rho_t(e_i) for the chosen item. The goal of the Recommender is to maximize their reward over T rounds subject to v_T satisfying H_c.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit linear optimization with contracting sets and perturbed actions
unmapped: Decision sets are nested (contracting) K_{t+1} subset of K_t; regret measured against the final set K_T
Played action is perturbed by unobserved adversarial vectors xi_t with norm <= eps
Observed loss phi_t in [0,1] is a noisy evaluation with E[phi_t] = f_t(y_t), f_t G-Lipschitz linear
settings.definition_quote: For a sequence of G-Lipschitz linear losses f_1,...,f_T and a contracting sequence of domains K_1,...,K_T (with K_j \subseteq K_i for j > i, each with diameter at most D, and where a ball of radius r > \delta+\epsilon around 0 is contained in K_T), and adversarially chosen unobserved vectors \xi_1,...,\xi_T with ||\xi_t|| <= \epsilon which perturb the chosen action at each step

settings.name_in_paper: Recommendation menus for adaptive agents (lower bound, known preference model)
unmapped: Agent choice probabilities depend on its memory vector of past choices through a preference model
Learner knows the preference model exactly (univariate linear score functions)
Benchmarks: best item distribution in IRD of the uniform vector, or best menu distribution
settings.definition_quote: There is no algorithm which can obtain o(T) regret against the best item distribution in the IRD set for the uniform vector, or against the best menu distribution in \Delta(n choose k), even when the preference model is known exactly and is expressible by univariate linear functions.

settings.name_in_paper: Online convex optimization over contracting decision sets (full information)
unmapped: Decision sets are nested (contracting); regret against the final set K_T
settings.definition_quote: For a sequence of contracting convex decision sets K_1,...,K_T, x_1 in K_1 each with diameter at most D, a sequence of G-Lipschitz losses l_1,...,l_T

algorithms.name: No-regret recommendation algorithm for adaptive agents (Algorithm 2)

conditions: benchmark: best item distribution in IRD(v_U, M) for the uniform memory vector
preference model known exactly, univariate linear score functions, lambda-dispersed

source.label: thm:regret-lowerbounds
source.quote: There is no algorithm which can obtain $o(T)$ regret against the best {item} distribution in the $\texttt{IRD}$ set for the uniform vector, or against the best { menu} distribution in $\Delta({n \choose k})$, even when the preference model is known exactly and is expressible by univariate linear functions.

results.notes: First half of Theorem 1 (proved as Lemma 5). Comparator is a fixed item distribution; expected reward used in the proof.

conditions: benchmark: best fixed menu distribution in Delta(n choose k)
preference model known exactly, univariate linear score functions, lambda-dispersed

source.label: thm:regret-lowerbounds
source.quote: There is no algorithm which can obtain $o(T)$ regret ... or against the best { menu} distribution in $\Delta({n \choose k})$, even when the preference model is known exactly and is expressible by univariate linear functions.

symbols.P_S: min over orderings sigma of the query set S of prod_{i=1}^{|S|-1} (1 + d_max(sigma(i), sigma(i+1))), d_max(v,v') = max_i v_i - v'_i

conditions: algorithms that produce a hypothesis by exact queries M(v) at each point v in a set S
Recommender can force the Agent to select any item and query M(v_t) at the current memory vector for free

source.label: thm:query-learning-lb
source.quote: Suppose the Recommender can force the Agent to select any item at each step $t$, and can query $M(v_t)$ at the current memory vector $v_t$. ... Then, any sequence of item selections and queries by the Recommender requires at least $T \geq \min_{\sigma \in \pi(S)} \prod_{i=1}^{|S|- 1} (1 + d_{\max}(\sigma(i), \sigma(i+1)) )$ rounds to run $\A(S)$

results.notes: Runtime (number of rounds) lower bound for query learning, not a regret bound. Implies (1+gamma)^m rounds for m pairwise gamma-separated points.

bound.expression_latex: n GDT^{3/4} + \frac{ G D T^{3/4}}{r} +  \frac{2 \epsilon GDT}{r}

symbols.eps_pert: norm bound on the adversarial perturbation of the played action

conditions: losses f_t are G-Lipschitz linear, observed loss phi_t in [0,1]
contracting decision sets each with diameter at most D
a ball of radius r > delta + eps around 0 is contained in K_T
unobserved adversarial perturbations with norm at most eps

source.quote: For a sequence of $G$-Lipschitz linear losses $f_1,\ldots,f_T$ and a contracting sequence of domains ... with parameters $\eta = \frac{D}{nT^{3/4}}$ and $\delta = \frac{1}{T^{1/4}}$, Algorithm 1 obtains the expected regret bound $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \E[\phi_t] - \min_{x \in \K_T} \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x) \leq n GDT^{3/4} + \frac{ G D T^{3/4}}{r} +  \frac{2 \epsilon GDT}{r}$.

results.notes: Paper's n is the dimension (mapped to d), G to L_lip, D to diam_K, r to r_K. Regret is E[sum phi_t] minus comparator losses via f_t (means), so pseudo-regret.

bound.expression_latex: \Tilde{O} ( t_0 + n GT^{3/4} + \frac{(\delta + \epsilon) G T}{r} + \epsilon GT) = \tilde{O}(T^{3/4})

conditions: preference model M is lambda-dispersed with lambda >= k^2/n
M belongs to a locally learnable class
score functions are L-Lipschitz
reward functions are G-Lipschitz linear
benchmark: best distribution in H_c intersected with EIRD(M)

source.label: thm:unif-regret
source.quote: Algorithm 2 obtains regret bounded by $\textup{Regret}_{C \cap \texttt{EIRD}(M)}(T) \leq \Tilde{O} ( t_0 + n GT^{3/4} + \frac{(\delta + \epsilon) G T}{r} + \epsilon GT) = \tilde{O}(T^{3/4})$ where $t_0$ is the time required for local learning, $r = O(k^2 / n)$, and $\epsilon, \delta = O(r \cdot T^{-1/4})$, and results in an empirical distribution such that $H_c$ is $O(\epsilon)$-satisfied with probability at least $1 - O(T^{-1/4})$.

results.notes: Regret type not precisely defined; proof bounds expected loss plus failure probabilities times T. PlayDist solves an LP over all (n choose k) menus, exponential in k. Also guarantees the diversity constraint is O(epsilon)-satisfied w.p. 1-O(T^{-1/4}). The O(T^{3/4}) rate assumes t_0 = O-tilde(T^{3/4}) (number of local-learning queries independent of error terms).

conditions: contracting convex decision sets with diameter at most D
G-Lipschitz convex losses
comparator in final set K_T

source.label: lemma:ogd-contracting
source.quote: For a sequence of contracting convex decision sets $\K_1, \ldots \K_T$, $x_1 \in \K_1$ each with diameter at most $D$, a sequence of $G$-Lipschitz losses $\ell_1,\ldots, \ell_T$, and $\eta = \frac{D}{G\sqrt{T}}$, the regret of Algorithm 3 with respect to $\K_t$ is bounded by $\sum_{t=1}^T \ell_t(x_t) - \min_{x^* \in \K_T }\sum_{t=1}^T \ell_t(x^*) \leq GD \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Deterministic full-information (gradient feedback) regret bound; convexity used in proof. The proof's derivation yields a factor 1/2 at intermediate steps but the lemma states GD sqrt(T).
